thesis: Cross-border AI use needs scoped conclusions for each operation, territory and date rather than a global clearance label.
role: Map international frameworks and selected national differences.

ideas.statement: Treaties coordinate national systems without a universal copyright or trademark; enforcement and target-market maps matter.
Training, lawful acquisition and output are separate acts; EU mining routes, AI-provider duties and voluntary codes do not collapse into a licence.
Romanian employment rules, Swiss categories, UK policy developments and Japanese non-enjoyment analysis require their own conditions and authority levels.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: A permissions matrix separates acquisition, storage, mining, retrieval, quotation, transformation and distribution.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: US procedural registration and remedies differ from existence of rights; agency reports are not enacted universal exceptions; incomplete vendor disclosure is not itself infringement proof.

audit.notes: Complete batch read; headings and navigation excluded from idea ranking.
